label: D2 after choosing a2, when the previous trial was unrewarded and not common
explanation: Fires only at D2 (100% of mass), only when this trial chose a2 (in_action = a2 at D2) and essentially only when the previous trial was unrewarded (99.8% of mass with prev_reward = 0). D2 & a2 & prev_reward == 0 alone gets recall 0.97 and mass recall 0.998 but precision 0.55. Adding prev_common != 1 (previous transition rare, or unknown because it falls before the window) raises precision to 0.80, F1 0.80 on dev, mass recall 0.97. Misses are mostly weak activations after a common unrewarded previous trial. Magnitude: the top activations are when a2 reaches S2 (common). Requiring state == 2 covers ~92-96% of the top two quartiles but only 38% of the second, so a2 -> S1 (rare) gives mid-sized activations. Magnitude also grows over runs of unrewarded a2 trials (e.g. 0.63 -> 0.68 -> 0.86 in one example). Never fires at D1/GO, after a1 choices, or after rewarded trials. All variables are observed at D2. prev_common == -1 is a window-edge artifact; the agent does know that transition.

issues: Factual claims check out on dev. 100% of activation mass is at D2 and 100% comes after an a2 choice. 0 active steps at D1 or GO. prev_reward==1 holds 0.2% of mass (1132 weak steps), and in_rew==1 has 0 actives. Reported test scores reproduce exactly: P 0.782, R 0.795, F1 0.788, mass recall 0.961.

'Not common' is broader than what the feature uses. Every previous-rare case that fires is a previous a2 that went to S1 rare and was unrewarded. With a previous a1 that went rare (prev_common==0 & prev_action==1), the predicate is true on 125 dev and 158 test steps and the feature is active on none of them (precision 0.0). This set is tiny, so the scores barely change, but the label should say 'stayed on a2 after a2 went to S1 (rare) and was unrewarded', not 'not common' in general.

The precision gap is systematic but comes from a window-edge artifact. When prev_common==-1 (the first trial in the window), precision is about 0.59: P 0.588 for prev_action==-1, P 0.622 when state==2. When the previous trial is known (prev_action==2 & prev_state==1), dev precision is 0.895 and test precision is 0.896. The window does not show the history behind the edge cases, so this cannot be fixed with window variables.

Missed activations after a common unrewarded a2 trial (prev_action==2 & prev_state==2) are real but weak: dev P 0.23, mass recall 0.023, mostly in the lowest activation quartile (0.55 coverage there, about 0 in Q3/Q4). This matches the explanation's 'misses are weak'.
Magnitude claims check out: adding state==2 covers [0.22, 0.38, 0.96, 0.92] by quartile, and state==1 covers mainly Q2 (0.56).

Test F1 0.788 is just below the 0.8 cutoff. The best observed-only refinement (requiring prev_action in {2,-1}) only reaches test F1 0.790, because the window edge sets a ceiling. No systematic counterexample class remains apart from that artifact.
